long_biography.plain_text:
Malouf entered Sydney's refuse trade soon after school, using a second-hand truck and limited capital. He drove collections himself and reinvested earnings in vehicles, transfer stations, materials processing and resource-recovery infrastructure. The local skip-bin operator grew into DADI, handling collection, landfill, recycling and recovered-product sales for domestic and commercial construction customers. Its vertical integration and processing capacity eventually attracted a strategic buyer.

Completion of the acquisition during 2019 moved DADI into Bingo's national network and gave Malouf a substantial listed shareholding plus a non-executive board seat. Macquarie-managed funds subsequently purchased Bingo, offering investors all-cash or mixed cash-and-unlisted-share consideration. Malouf later organized new capital deployment through a private investment trust and the Malouf Family Group. These vehicles undertake direct deals and commercial partnerships spanning more than one industry.

Service is used for wealth creation because Dial-a-Dump earned through waste collection, transfer, recycling, resource recovery and disposal. The taxonomy has no dedicated waste-management category.

Finance and Investments is the best-supported current industry because Malouf describes a family office and multiple joint ventures, and a current Malouf investment trust is registered. No single post-exit operating sector is sufficiently dominant to replace that classification.

Family office principal describes Malouf's current relationship to the capital after the Dial-a-Dump exit. Founder remains his enduring relationship to the original wealth-producing company but is not the best description of the present investment structure.

Self-made — independent start reflects the single used truck and limited starting capital described in interviews. No inherited operating asset or substantial family-business platform was identified, though the exact source of every dollar of launch capital is not documented in transaction filings.
The Bingo sale was announced in 2018 and completed in 2019. The biographies use the completion year because that is when Dial-a-Dump transferred and Malouf received the cash-and-share consideration.

The later Bingo takeover offered shareholders either cash or mixed cash-and-unlisted-share consideration. Malouf's individual election and any continuing beneficial interest are not established, so the dossier does not attribute either outcome to him.

Bingo reports Malouf as a non-executive director through its 2023 report period. No sufficiently current governance source established whether that board role continues in 2026, so it is not presented as a current title.

Malouf Family Group and the registered investment trust support a current family-office structure, but public records do not reveal a complete portfolio or reliable sector allocation. Specific medical, property, waste-related and leisure holdings are therefore not attributed in the biographies.
